findings.message: Paths are decoded two different ways. `find_root` uses `errors="surrogateescape"` so that a path round-trips. `git()` uses `errors="replace"`, and it also returns paths (for example `diff --name-only -z`, or any output when `core.quotePath=false`). A path read through `git()` that contains a byte which is not valid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD, and a later `git checkout -- <path>` in `_run_tests` will not match the file. Fix: pick one error policy for path-bearing git output, or document that `git()` output is display-only. Not raised to major: with git's default `core.quotePath=true`, non-ASCII paths are octal-quoted, so no default-config scenario was shown.

The `call_backend` and `_run_tests` checks go through a hand-written `Cfg` stub instead of a real `rc.Config`. If `Config.get` or `Config.num` change shape, the stub stays green. Fix: build a real config from a temporary `.specclaw/config.yaml`, which `rc.Config(d)` already supports.

On Linux and macOS, the `find_root` assertion (`basename == 'café'`) passes with or without the change, because the locale is already UTF-8. Only the 0x8f rows prove anything there. Add a note, or a row that fails on POSIX without `encoding=` (for example, run under `LC_ALL=C` / `PYTHONIOENCODING` unset with `PYTHONUTF8=0`).

The `ln -s` calls for `$TMP/v/presets/dotnet.md` and `b.md` (and the dangling case now has `2>/dev/null`, these do not) still print to stderr on Git Bash when no real symlink is made. The checks behind them are skipped, so this is noise, not a wrong result. Fix: add `2>/dev/null` to match, or guard the setup with `[ -n "$SYM" ]`.

Only stdout was made LF-only. Error lines that go to stderr through text-mode `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` still get `\r\n` on Windows. Callers that compare stderr text could differ by OS. This is low impact because tests discard stderr. Fix: write stderr the same way, or reconfigure both streams once with `sys.stdout.reconfigure(newline='\n')` so there is no second copy of the rule.
